classification.difficultyReason: Construct the requested circle, chord and tangent, identify the alternate segment, and apply the stated equal-angle relationship twice.

content.prompt: Draw a large circle and a chord AB. At one end of the chord, draw the tangent to the circle.

spec.description: Source inscribed triangle ABC and tangent at A. Theta between AB and downward tangent ray; alpha between AC and upward tangent ray. Tangent endpoints intentionally unlabelled as source.
spec.answerVisibility: Original supplied givens and targets only; no derived numerical values or proof conclusions.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Mark one of the angles θ between the tangent and the chord AB, then draw any angle in the alternate segment. How are these two angles related?

answer.worked: Draw a circle, chord AB and the tangent at A. Choose C in the alternate segment and join AC and BC. The alternate segment theorem gives $\angle ACB=\theta$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Mark the angle α between the tangent and the chord AC. Which angle is equal to α?

answer.worked: For chord AC, the angle at B lies in the alternate segment, so $\angle ABC=\alpha$ (alternate segment theorem).
